one_liner: Pre-block transaction scheduler on revm and QMDB claiming 1.1M Merkleized ETH transfers/s on 96 cores; no sequential baseline.
what_it_does: FAFO reorders mempool transactions before block formation so that non-conflicting ones execute in parallel on revm, while the bundled QMDB Merkleizes world state after every block. It is a whole execution pipeline (the exepipe crate: simulator, framer, dispatcher, block context) rather than a per-transaction library: you hand ExePipe::run_block_with_sim a block as Vec<Vec<Box<Tx>>> of revm TxEnv values. The only driver in the repo is bench-sendeth, a synthetic ETH/ERC-20 transfer replay harness; there is no integration with reth, geth or any node.
how_it_is_fast: ParaLyze pre-executes a transaction on revm against current state to predict its read and write sets as 80-bit short hashes of accounts and storage slots. ParaFramer packs 4-transaction tasks into up to 64 frames (Framer<u64>) using ParaBloom, a per-frame Bloom-filter bitmap, so tasks inside a frame never conflict; the dispatcher runs frames on a 64-thread rayon pool with 12 warm-up (prefetch) threads, i.e. deterministic scheduling from predicted access sets instead of optimistic execute-and-validate as in Block-STM. Any transaction that touches state outside its predicted set is dropped by the access check, and QMDB's append-only Merkle storage keeps per-block root computation cheap on NVMe.
when_to_use: Prototyping or researching a high-throughput EVM-compatible sequencer or rollup node where you control the whole execution stack and can run a many-core server with large NVMe storage.
Workloads dominated by native ETH and ERC-20 transfers spread over many accounts with low contention, which is the only shape the repo benchmarks.
When a state commitment per block is required at high throughput (light clients, stateless or ZK validation) and you are willing to adopt QMDB as the state store.
As a reference implementation of Bloom-filter conflict framing to compare against Block-STM style executors (pevm) on your own traces.
when_not_to_use: You want a faster executor inside an existing client: there is no reth/geth integration, no crates.io release (exepipe is publish = false), and the code is a single 'Initial commit' marked ongoing research.

You need exact Ethereum semantics: both run_tx and run_tx_with_disable_nonce_check pass disable_nonce_check = true, MpexHandler skips the beneficiary reward, and any EVM error other than an access-set violation hits handle_tx_execute_mpex_err, which is panic!("not implemented").
Contract-heavy or hot-contract traffic: nothing beyond plain transfers is benchmarked, and the README itself says gains are bounded by contention (hotn generator).

Small machines: the paper-size run initialises 2^30 accounts, the README asks for at least 256 GB of Docker virtual disk and 32 GB of memory, and thread pools are compile-time constants (12 warm-up, 64 execution, 16 simulation threads).
You need a maintained dependency: no commits since 2025-06-26, issues are restricted to collaborators, and the only pull request is an open typo fix.

integration.form: source-drop (Cargo workspace: exepipe, exepipe-common, codedb, hpfile, bench-sendeth, with QMDB vendored in-tree; not published to crates.io)
integration.dependencies: revm 20.0.0, alloy 0.11.1, rayon, crossbeam, threadpool, parking_lot, dashmap (workspace pins); QMDB in-tree; tikv-jemallocator on Linux for the benchmark binary
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.85.0 pinned in rust-toolchain.toml, edition 2021; .cargo/config.toml adds --cfg const_slice_from_raw_parts_mut
integration.platforms: Linux recommended (README steers users to a VS Code Dev Container; jemalloc is Linux-gated); other platforms not documented
integration.thread_safety: Internally multi-threaded; ExePipe::run_block_with_sim takes &mut self and processes one block at a time, with hard-coded pool sizes
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false: a whole-block pipeline over its own QMDB state store, not a replacement for revm's executor or Database trait, and not comparable to sequential revm without porting state

gotchas: Harness flaw (bench-sendeth/src/common/parallel_transfer.rs): ERC-20 runs attach precomputed write sets (the sender and receiver balance slots) to 99 of every 100 transactions (no_rwsets_pct = 1), so the revm pre-execution ParaLyze needs in production runs for only 1% of the measured ERC-20 transactions; native ETH runs skip it entirely because SimulatorShard gives every empty-calldata transaction an empty CrwSets (commented 'TODO: need review'), which is correct for EOA-to-EOA transfers but would mis-schedule a value transfer into a contract whose receive() or fallback writes storage.

Throughput is transfer_txn_count divided by replay wall time: it counts transactions handed to the framer (the only assertion is framer.txns_processed == transfer_txn_count), never checks execution results, and every transaction carries nonce 0, gas price 0, a default hash and no signature, so signature recovery, nonce checks and fee accounting are absent from the measured path.

Paper-size runs use huge blocks: the full ETH preset (30 bits) replays 32 blocks of 2^20 = 1,048,576 transfers (2^25 in total) and the ERC-20 preset 256 blocks of 131,072, so 'Merkleizing every block' amortises one state root over about a million transfers; init-db and the database copy are excluded from the timed region.

Thread counts are fixed in source (Dispatcher::new(12, 64), ThreadPool::new(16), 4 simulator shards) with no CLI flag, so reproducing the 'near-linear scaling to 96 cores' curve needs code edits; the workspace Cargo.toml declares license MIT while the README and LICENSE files say MIT OR Apache-2.0.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: risechain/pevm is the closer sibling: Block-STM style optimistic parallel execution on revm with published sequential-revm baselines (22.1x on Uniswap swaps on Graviton3); pick FAFO only if you want deterministic pre-block framing plus per-block Merkleization on a large node and can live with research code. For single-thread EVM speed, revm, evmone or revmc are the relevant entries.
verified_claims_summary: The README and LayerZero Labs' own preprint (arXiv 2507.10757, 'Under submission', read only as search-result text) claim over 1.1 million native ETH transfers and over 0.5 million ERC-20 transfers per second on a 96-core server while Merkleizing every block, plus 91% lower cost than unnamed 'state-of-the-art sharded execution'; the repo has the bench-sendeth harness but no result files, no hardware, and no sequential revm, pevm or Block-STM run. Reading the harness shows those runs use million-transaction blocks, oracle write sets for 99% of ERC-20 transactions and no nonce or signature checks, so the figures are an upper bound for transfer-only traffic, not a like-for-like speedup over revm.
status_note: Stale research drop (one 'Initial commit' on 2025-06-26, 65 stars, issues closed to the public) under MIT OR Apache-2.0; useful as a reference design, not as a production executor.
sources_read: WebSearch: FAFO 1 million TPS EVM Merkleizing paper (result text for arXiv 2507.10757 and layerzero.network/research/fafo; pages not opened)
